sections.h2: Who to call about Hillsborough County property tax
sections.html:
The right office depends on the question. Value and exemptions belong to the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser. Money, receipts and payment plans belong to the Hillsborough County Tax Collector.

The appraiser's downtown Tampa office is on the 15th floor of the County Center, 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard, and answers at (813) 272-6100 Monday through Friday from 8 to 5. The collector's real estate tax page has bills, payment options and a property search. Disputes over value or exemptions go to the Value Adjustment Board, which is separate from both offices.

  • Property Appraiser: just value, homestead filings, the assessment cap, portability and the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, installment applications, partial payments and tax certificates.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: recorded deeds, liens and the tax deed auction.

The appraiser also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that flags new recordings made in your name. Heirs who hold an empty Tampa Bay house are the people most likely to want it turned on.

sections.h2: How does the bill and early payment discount work?
sections.html:
Tax notices arrive in November and can be paid beginning November 1. An account still open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

Early payers save 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February, and March is full price. A winter seller should ask the closing agent which month the closing date lands in, since sale proceeds may be what pays the bill.

For smaller checks, the installment plan requires an application before May 1 and begins with a June payment. A July payment keeps the plan alive but loses the discount. If nothing is received by July 31, the account leaves the plan and the whole balance is payable the next November, with the 4 percent break. A separate partial payment option exists for current-year bills only. An overdue real estate account must be cleared in one payment.

sections.h2: Dates to put on your calendar
sections.html:
Seven dates drive nearly every decision a Hillsborough County owner or seller faces.

WhenWhat it triggers
January 1Valuation date and homestead test date
March 1Exemption filing deadline
May 1Last day to request the installment plan
By June 1Online auction of tax certificates
AugustTRIM notice mailed, then 25 days to petition on value
November 1Bills payable
April 1Delinquency

An owner whose exemption is refused receives an Official Notice of Denial by July 1, which opens the right to a hearing before a Value Adjustment Board magistrate.

A permanent residence can shed up to $50,000 of assessed value in two layers. The first layer touches every levy. The second sits on the slice of assessed value above $50,000 and skips school taxes. After the first year, a yearly growth limit applies. The appraiser accepts filings year round, treats March 1 as the legal deadline, and may take a late one up to 25 days after TRIM notices go out.

  • Low income senior: unincorporated Hillsborough County and the City of Tampa allow up to $50,000, and Temple Terrace allows up to $25,000.
  • Long term resident senior: Tampa and unincorporated areas, for homes with just value under $250,000 and 25 consecutive years in residence.
  • Veteran, disability, widow and blind exemptions: these need documents, and the county's veteran affairs office, at 813-635-8316, helps with discharge papers.

Claiming homestead on a house you have left is costly. The exempted taxes from the prior 10 years can turn into a lien with a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest, so report a move-out before the sign goes in the yard.

sections.h2: What did Amendment 3 change for homesteads?
sections.html:
Voters passed the statewide property tax amendment on November 3, 2026. The appraiser's legislative update page describes homestead exemption amounts of up to $150,000 from 2027 and up to $250,000 from 2028, with lawmakers directed to schedule further increases. The effect varies by parcel and cannot be calculated in advance, so treat the figure on today's bill as your working number until a TRIM notice shows a new one. The tax collector keeps a property tax reform page on the same ballot item.

Sellers mostly feel this through the buyer. The first bill after a purchase starts from just value, and a new exemption amount reaches the buyer only after an application is filed.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax when a house closes?
sections.html:
An open bill is settled from the seller's proceeds at the table, because the lien stays with the land. The name printed on a bill is no obstacle to paying it, since a recorded deed may not have reached the appraiser before the roll was certified.

The seller's homestead ends with the sale, and the buyer starts at just value after the next January 1 with a new application. What the seller can carry along is the portable savings, which attach to a replacement home.

  • Escrowed loans: the servicer pays from a list it sends the collector, and once the loan is paid off the next bill is mailed to the owner.
  • Deed stamps: the state rate applies here because Hillsborough is not Miami-Dade, and each party on the deed shares the liability.
  • Portability: the replacement homestead has a three year window and needs a DR-501T with the new application.

Plain preparation helps. Ask the title agent to request the payoff from the collector close to the closing date. Check earlier years for balances as well as the current bill. A cash buyer needs no lender sign-off, so a payoff taken from your proceeds does not hold up funding.

sections.h2: How unpaid tax reaches a tax deed sale
sections.html:
A skipped bill becomes a tax certificate first, and a deed sale can follow about two years later.

The collector auctions certificates online. Bids start at 18 percent and fall by 0.25 percent per step, and the lowest bidder wins a certificate that ranks first among liens, including other government ones. A deed application cannot begin until up to 22 months after issue, and the statute measures two years from April 1 of the issue year. When a homestead owes under $250, the county takes the certificate itself and no investor can buy it.

The clerk conducts the deed auction, and a homestead parcel's opening bid includes half of the last assessed value. An owner who is behind can still sell, since paying off the certificate at closing clears the title.

faqs.q: When is Hillsborough County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are payable November 1 and go delinquent April 1. The discount is 4 percent in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February. An account open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hillsborough County tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if you apply before May 1. The first payment is due in June, a July payment keeps you in the plan without the discount, and missing July 31 drops the account into a single November payment with the 4 percent discount.

faqs.q: Who decides a Hillsborough County homestead claim?
faqs.a: The Property Appraiser. Filing closes March 1, any denial notice is mailed by July 1, and an appeal goes to the Value Adjustment Board. The collector never rules on eligibility.

faqs.q: Are partial payments allowed on a delinquent Hillsborough County bill?
faqs.a: No. Only current-year bills qualify for the partial plan, and an overdue real estate bill needs the full balance. Call the collector before sending anything smaller.

faqs.q: What if I sell before my Hillsborough County bill arrives?
faqs.a: The bill is still paid at closing. The title agent requests the amount from the collector and takes it out of the seller's money, and the buyer applies for a new homestead by the next March 1.
